<!-- Shared setup for Master_Summary_Report.qmd and SC_GEX_Report.qmd: libraries, table
     access, interactive helpers and every module table, loaded once. -->

```{r}
#| label: setup
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(data.table)
  library(dplyr)
  library(tidyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(forcats)
  library(scales)
  library(plotly)
  library(reactable)
  library(htmltools)
})

dir.create(file.path(params$outdir, "tables"),  recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(file.path(params$outdir, "figures"), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (!is.null(a) && length(a) > 0 && !all(is.na(a))) a else b

# ── Input access ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Every upstream module stages its tables under <tables_dir>/<module>/. A module that
# did not run on this route simply has no directory, so T() returns NULL and the
# corresponding section renders an explanatory note rather than silently nothing.
T <- function(module, name) {
  p <- file.path(params$tables_dir, module, name)
  if (!file.exists(p) || file.size(p) == 0) return(NULL)
  out <- tryCatch({
    if (tolower(tools::file_ext(name)) == "csv") fread(p) else fread(p, sep = "\t")
  }, error = function(e) NULL)
  if (is.null(out) || nrow(out) == 0) return(NULL)
  as.data.frame(out)
}

# `-P label_col=` (an empty params.label_col) reaches R as NULL, and nzchar(NULL) is
# logical(0), which makes if() error rather than return FALSE. Normalise every incoming
# string param to a length-1 character before testing it.
as_str1 <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0) return("")
  x <- as.character(x)[1]
  if (is.na(x)) "" else trimws(x)
}

# Count distinct values, ignoring NA and empty strings (a blank column otherwise counts
# as one value).
n_distinct_real <- function(x) {
  if (is.null(x)) return(NA_integer_)
  x <- trimws(as.character(x))
  x <- x[!is.na(x) & nzchar(x)]
  if (!length(x)) return(NA_integer_)
  length(unique(x))
}

have <- function(x) !is.null(x) && nrow(x) > 0

note <- function(txt) knitr::asis_output(paste0("\n::: {.callout-note appearance=\"simple\"}\n",
                                                txt, "\n:::\n\n"))

# Per-figure TSVs only with --write_figure_tables: the figures are views of the core tables
# in results/ (RESULTS_EXPORT), so writing each one again is redundant.
write_fig_tables <- isTRUE(as.logical(params$write_figure_tables %||% FALSE))
save_table <- function(df, filename) {
  if (write_fig_tables && have(df)) fwrite(df, file.path(params$outdir, "tables", filename), sep = "\t")
  invisible(df)
}

theme_ms <- function(base_size = params$base_size) {
  theme_bw(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = base_size + 1, hjust = 0),
      axis.title      = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(linewidth = 0.2, color = "grey90"),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = "grey80"),
      strip.text      = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.title    = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
}

# ── Interactive output helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────
# Figures are built with plot_ly() directly rather than ggplotly(). The container pairs
# ggplot2 4.0.2 with plotly 4.10.4, and that plotly predates ggplot2's 4.x internals, so
# ggplotly() dies with "subscript out of bounds" on most plots. Native plot_ly() calls do
# not touch ggplot internals and are version-robust.
#
# Every figure supports: hover for exact values, drag to zoom, double-click to reset,
# click legend entries to toggle series.
pal <- c("#2c7fb8", "#d95f02", "#7570b3", "#1b9e77",
         "#e7298a", "#66a61e", "#e6ab02", "#a6761d")

pconf <- function(p) {
  plotly::config(p, displaylogo = FALSE,
                 modeBarButtonsToRemove = c("select2d", "lasso2d"),
                 toImageButtonOptions = list(format = "png", scale = 2))
}

ttl <- function(t) list(text = t, x = 0, xanchor = "left",
                        font = list(size = params$base_size + 4))

# Horizontal bar. df: cat (chr), val (num), hover (chr)
hbar <- function(df, title, xlab, colour = "#2c7fb8", height = 440, tickformat = NULL) {
  df <- df[order(df$val), , drop = FALSE]
  df$cat <- factor(df$cat, levels = unique(df$cat))
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(df, x = ~val, y = ~cat, type = "bar", orientation = "h", textposition = "none",
                        marker = list(color = colour),
                        text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
        plotly::layout(title = ttl(title), height = height,
                       margin = list(l = 140, t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = xlab, tickformat = tickformat),
                       yaxis = list(title = "")))
}

# Stacked horizontal bar. df: cat, val, grp, hover
sbar <- function(df, title, xlab, height = 470, tickformat = ".0%", colors = pal, legend_title = "") {
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(df, x = ~val, y = ~cat, color = ~grp, colors = colors,
                        type = "bar", orientation = "h", textposition = "none",
                        text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
        plotly::layout(barmode = "stack", title = ttl(title), height = height,
                       margin = list(l = 140, t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = xlab, tickformat = tickformat),
                       yaxis = list(title = ""),
                       # On the right: a horizontal legend under a short chart collides
                       # with the axis title.
                       legend = list(orientation = "v", x = 1.02, y = 1, yanchor = "top",
                                     title = list(text = legend_title))))
}

# Grouped vertical bar. df: cat, val, grp, hover
gbar <- function(df, title, xlab, ylab, height = 470) {
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(df, x = ~cat, y = ~val, color = ~grp, colors = pal,
                        type = "bar", textposition = "none",
                        text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
        plotly::layout(barmode = "group", title = ttl(title), height = height,
                       margin = list(t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = xlab), yaxis = list(title = ylab),
                       legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2)))
}

# Box plot with points. df: grp, val, hover
boxby <- function(df, title, ylab, height = 470, logy = FALSE, angle = 0) {
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(df, x = ~grp, y = ~val, color = ~grp, colors = pal,
                        type = "box", boxpoints = "all", jitter = 0.4, pointpos = 0,
                        marker = list(size = 4, opacity = 0.55),
                        text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text") %>%
        plotly::layout(title = ttl(title), height = height, showlegend = FALSE,
                       margin = list(t = 60, b = 110),
                       xaxis = list(title = "", tickangle = angle),
                       yaxis = list(title = ylab,
                                    type = if (logy) "log" else "linear")))
}

# Scatter. df: x, y, grp, hover  (grp may be a constant)
scat <- function(df, title, xlab, ylab, height = 470, size = 11) {
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(df, x = ~x, y = ~y, color = ~grp, colors = pal,
                        type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
                        marker = list(size = size, opacity = 0.85),
                        text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
        plotly::layout(title = ttl(title), height = height, margin = list(t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = xlab), yaxis = list(title = ylab)))
}

# Line/step. df: x, y, grp, hover
lplot <- function(df, title, xlab, ylab, logx = TRUE, logy = TRUE, height = 470) {
  pconf(plotly::plot_ly(df, x = ~x, y = ~y, color = ~grp, colors = pal,
                        type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
                        text = ~hover, hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>") %>%
        plotly::layout(title = ttl(title), height = height, margin = list(t = 60),
                       xaxis = list(title = xlab, type = if (logx) "log" else "linear"),
                       yaxis = list(title = ylab, type = if (logy) "log" else "linear")))
}

# ── Per-patient tabs ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One tab per key (patient), in the same `::: {.panel-tabset}` layout as the report
# notebooks' per-patient figures; a single key renders without a tab bar. render(key)
# returns a widget or tagList. Each panel goes through knit_child so its htmlwidget
# dependencies reach the page (a widget printed inside a loop would lose them). Call
# from a chunk with `results: asis`.
patient_tabs <- function(keys, render, level = "####") {
  .knit_one <- function(obj) {
    .tab_obj <- obj
    knitr::knit_child(text = c("```{r}", "#| echo: false", ".tab_obj", "```"),
                      envir = environment(), quiet = TRUE)
  }
  keys <- as.character(keys)
  if (!length(keys)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (length(keys) == 1) { cat(.knit_one(render(keys[1])), "\n\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }
  cat("::: {.panel-tabset}\n\n")
  for (k in keys) cat(level, " ", k, "\n\n", .knit_one(render(k)), "\n\n", sep = "")
  cat(":::\n\n")
  invisible(NULL)
}

# Numbered caption under a figure outside the GEX section ("Figure T1."). text is HTML.
figcap <- function(w, label, title, text = "") {
  if (inherits(w, "plotly")) {
    w <- plotly::plotly_build(w)
    if (!is.null(w$x$layout$height)) w$height <- w$x$layout$height
  }
  htmltools::tagList(w, htmltools::tags$p(style = "margin-top: 0.5rem;",
    htmltools::HTML(sprintf("<strong>Figure %s. %s.</strong> %s", label, title, text))))
}

# ── Clone tracking (alluvial) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Clone-level share of each sample, the patient's top clones stacked at the bottom of every
# bar and joined between consecutive samples by ribbons. Used by the TCR-only view (from
# CLONAL_DYNAMICS clonotypes) and the phenotype view (from the per-cell export).
#   fr   : data.frame(key, sample, pct)      - a clone's % of the sample; keys = top clones
#   smp  : data.frame(sample, label, hover)  - samples in plotting order
#   keys : top clone keys, rank order (1 = largest peak)
#   seg  : optional data.frame(key, sample, state, frac) - each block's split by cell
#          state (key "rest" for the other clones); NULL draws one colour per clone
#   clone_cols  : colour per key (TCR-only blocks and every ribbon)
#   state_cols_ : colour per state (when seg is given)
#   key_text    : legend / hover label per key
track_slate <- c("#1f2d3d", "#34485e", "#4c6279", "#667d94", "#8399ad", "#a2b4c4",
                 "#b8c6d3", "#cbd6df", "#dbe3ea", "#e8edf2")
track_rest  <- "#e6e5e0"

track_plot <- function(fr, smp, keys, clone_cols, key_text, title, seg = NULL,
                       state_cols_ = NULL, height = 520, unit = "cells") {
  n  <- nrow(smp); w <- 0.42
  pct <- matrix(0, length(keys), n, dimnames = list(keys, smp$sample))
  ok <- fr$key %in% keys & fr$sample %in% smp$sample
  pct[cbind(as.character(fr$key[ok]), as.character(fr$sample[ok]))] <- fr$pct[ok]
  lo <- apply(pct, 2, function(v) cumsum(v) - v)          # lower edge of each block
  if (!is.matrix(lo)) lo <- matrix(lo, nrow = length(keys), dimnames = dimnames(pct))
  top <- colSums(pct)
  p <- plotly::plot_ly()
  # Ribbons: one smooth band per clone between consecutive samples, and one for the rest.
  tt <- seq(0, 1, length.out = 30); sm <- 3 * tt^2 - 2 * tt^3
  band <- function(p, x0, x1, a0, b0, a1, b1, col, alpha) {
    xs <- x0 + (x1 - x0) * tt
    lo_ <- a0 + (a1 - a0) * sm; hi_ <- b0 + (b1 - b0) * sm
    plotly::add_trace(p, x = c(xs, rev(xs)), y = c(hi_, rev(lo_)), type = "scatter", mode = "lines",
                      fill = "toself", fillcolor = plotly::toRGB(col, alpha),
                      line = list(color = "white", width = 0.8), hoverinfo = "skip",
                      showlegend = FALSE, inherit = FALSE)
  }
  if (n > 1) for (s in seq_len(n - 1)) {
    x0 <- s - 1 + w / 2; x1 <- s - w / 2
    for (k in keys) {
      if (pct[k, s] == 0 && pct[k, s + 1] == 0) next
      p <- band(p, x0, x1, lo[k, s], lo[k, s] + pct[k, s], lo[k, s + 1], lo[k, s + 1] + pct[k, s + 1],
                clone_cols[[k]], if (is.null(seg)) 0.42 else 0.32)
    }
    p <- band(p, x0, x1, top[s], 100, top[s + 1], 100, track_rest, 0.55)
  }
  # Bars, as stacked blocks with an explicit base so each block sits where its ribbon ends.
  blk <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(n), function(s) rbind(
    data.frame(key = keys, s = s, y0 = lo[, s], h = pct[, s], stringsAsFactors = FALSE),
    data.frame(key = "rest", s = s, y0 = top[s], h = 100 - top[s], stringsAsFactors = FALSE))))
  blk <- blk[blk$h > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  blk$lab  <- ifelse(blk$key == "rest", "All other clones", key_text[blk$key])
  blk$where <- smp$hover[blk$s]
  if (is.null(seg)) {
    for (k in c(keys, "rest")) {
      b <- blk[blk$key == k, , drop = FALSE]
      if (!nrow(b)) next
      p <- plotly::add_bars(p, x = b$s - 1, y = b$h, base = b$y0, width = w, name = b$lab[1],
                            marker = list(color = if (k == "rest") track_rest else clone_cols[[k]],
                                          line = list(color = "white", width = 1)),
                            text = paste0(b$lab, "<br>", b$where, "<br>", sprintf("%.1f%%", b$h), " of the sample"),
                            hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>", textposition = "none",
                            legendgroup = k, inherit = FALSE)
    }
  } else {
    # Each block split by the cell states of its cells in that sample.
    sg <- merge(blk, transform(seg, s = match(sample, smp$sample))[, c("key", "s", "state", "frac")],
                by = c("key", "s"))
    sg <- sg[order(sg$s, match(sg$key, c(keys, "rest")), match(sg$state, names(state_cols_))), ]
    sg$h2 <- sg$h * sg$frac
    sg$b2 <- ave(sg$h2, sg$s, sg$key, FUN = function(v) cumsum(v) - v) + sg$y0
    for (st in intersect(names(state_cols_), unique(sg$state))) {
      b <- sg[sg$state == st, , drop = FALSE]
      p <- plotly::add_bars(p, x = b$s - 1, y = b$h2, base = b$b2, width = w, name = st,
                            marker = list(color = state_cols_[[st]], line = list(width = 0)),
                            text = paste0(b$lab, "<br>", b$where, "<br>", st, ": ",
                                          sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * b$frac), " of the block (",
                                          sprintf("%.1f%%", b$h2), " of the sample)"),
                            hovertemplate = "%{text}<extra></extra>", textposition = "none",
                            legendgroup = st, inherit = FALSE)
    }
    # White outline around each clone's block, so the stacked states read as one block.
    p <- plotly::layout(p, shapes = lapply(seq_len(nrow(blk)), function(i) list(
      type = "rect", xref = "x", yref = "y", x0 = blk$s[i] - 1 - w / 2, x1 = blk$s[i] - 1 + w / 2,
      y0 = blk$y0[i], y1 = blk$y0[i] + blk$h[i], line = list(color = "white", width = 1.2),
      fillcolor = "rgba(0,0,0,0)")))
  }
  # Each clone's number on its peak bar, so identity never rests on colour alone.
  ann <- lapply(seq_along(keys), function(i) {
    s <- which.max(pct[keys[i], ])
    if (pct[keys[i], s] < 1.5) return(NULL)
    list(x = s - 1, y = lo[keys[i], s] + pct[keys[i], s] / 2, text = paste0("<b>", i, "</b>"),
         showarrow = FALSE, font = list(color = "white", size = 12), xref = "x", yref = "y")
  })
  sized(pconf(plotly::layout(p, barmode = "overlay", title = ttl(title), height = height,
                       margin = list(t = 60, b = 90),
                       xaxis = list(title = "", tickmode = "array", tickvals = seq_len(n) - 1,
                                    ticktext = smp$label, range = c(-0.6, n - 0.4), zeroline = FALSE,
                                    showgrid = FALSE),
                       yaxis = list(title = paste0("Share of the sample's ", unit), range = c(0, 100),
                                    ticksuffix = "%", showgrid = FALSE, zeroline = FALSE),
                       annotations = Filter(Negate(is.null), ann),
                       legend = list(orientation = "v", x = 1.02, y = 1, yanchor = "top",
                                     traceorder = "normal",
                                     title = list(text = if (is.null(seg)) "Top clones (CDR3β)" else "Cell state")))))
}

# A plotly widget placed inside a tagList takes the chunk's default height rather than its
# layout's: build it and carry the layout height over (as withcap() does).
sized <- function(p) {
  w <- plotly::plotly_build(p)
  if (!is.null(w$x$layout$height)) w$height <- w$x$layout$height
  w
}

# Clone key list (number, CDR3β, detail) shown under a tracking figure.
clone_key_html <- function(keys, cdr3, detail, cols) {
  items <- vapply(seq_along(keys), function(i) sprintf(
    paste0('<span style="display:inline-block;margin:0 1.2rem 0.3rem 0;">',
           '<span style="display:inline-block;width:1.2em;text-align:center;color:white;',
           'background:%s;font-weight:600;border-radius:2px;margin-right:0.35rem;">%d</span>',
           '<code>%s</code> <span style="color:#52514e;">%s</span></span>'),
    cols[[keys[i]]], i, htmltools::htmlEscape(cdr3[i]), htmltools::htmlEscape(detail[i])), character(1))
  paste(items, collapse = "")
}

itable <- function(df, caption = NULL, pageSize = 10, ...) {
  if (!have(df)) return(note("No data available."))
  # Whole-number columns (counts) without decimals; other numbers to 3 digits.
  counts <- names(df)[vapply(df, function(x) is.numeric(x) && all(is.na(x) | x == round(x)), logical(1))]
  cols <- setNames(lapply(counts, function(c) colDef(format = colFormat(digits = 0, separators = TRUE))), counts)
  reactable(
    columns = if (length(cols)) cols else NULL,
    df,
    searchable = TRUE, sortable = TRUE, filterable = FALSE,
    highlight = TRUE, compact = TRUE, striped = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = pageSize, showPageSizeOptions = TRUE,
    pageSizeOptions = c(5, 10, 25, 50, 100),
    defaultColDef = colDef(
      format = colFormat(digits = 3),
      minWidth = 90,
      headerStyle = list(background = "#f7f7f8", fontWeight = 600)
    ),
    ...
  )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: load-all
# Only the tables the Master Summary still renders: consensus clustering and the GEX
# section. The run-level QC, repertoire, overlap and sequence-clustering tables moved with
# their sections to the QC & Run Info and Details reports.

# ── GEX-dependent ──
tcell_roll     <- T("tcell", "tcell_summary_rollup.tsv")
conga_roll     <- T("conga", "conga_summary_rollup.tsv")
conga_clusters <- T("conga", "conga_cluster_summary.tsv")
cons_roll      <- T("consensus", "consensus_summary_rollup.tsv")
tcri_roll      <- T("tcri", "tcri_summary_rollup.tsv")
tcri_scores    <- T("tcri", "high_tcri_clone_summary.tsv")
cons_clusters  <- T("consensus", "consensus_cluster_summary.tsv")

# ── Per-cell export ──
export_cells <- NULL
.ec <- as_str1(params$export_cells_file)
if (nzchar(.ec) && file.exists(.ec) && file.size(.ec) > 0) {
  export_cells <- tryCatch(as.data.frame(fread(.ec, sep = "\t")),
                           error = function(e) NULL)
}

pick_col <- function(df, preferred, candidates) {
  if (is.null(df) || !ncol(df)) return(NULL)
  preferred <- as_str1(preferred)
  cand <- trimws(unlist(strsplit(gsub('"', "", as_str1(candidates)), ";", fixed = TRUE)))
  cand <- cand[nzchar(cand)]
  if (nzchar(preferred) && preferred %in% names(df)) return(preferred)
  hit <- intersect(cand, names(df))
  if (length(hit)) hit[[1]] else NULL
}
sample_col  <- pick_col(export_cells, params$sample_col,  params$sample_candidates)
patient_col <- pick_col(export_cells, params$patient_col, params$patient_candidates)
label_col   <- pick_col(export_cells, params$label_col,   params$label_candidates)
clone_col   <- pick_col(export_cells, params$clone_id_col, params$clone_id_candidates)
cons_col    <- pick_col(export_cells, params$consensus_cluster_col, params$consensus_cluster_candidates)

has_gex <- !is.null(tcell_roll) || !is.null(cons_roll) || !is.null(conga_roll) || !is.null(tcri_roll)
is_bulk <- identical(tolower(as_str1(params$modality)), "bulk")
route   <- if (is_bulk) "Bulk TCR repertoire (clonotype-level; no cells)" else
           if (has_gex) "Full single-cell (GEX + VDJ)" else "VDJ-only (no GEX object)"
```
